newsitem.title: GERMANY: Moevenpick sees higher profits in 1996 and beyond.
newsitem.headline: Moevenpick sees higher profits in 1996 and beyond.

text.p: Swiss food and hotel group Moevenpick said it expected to post higher profits for 1996 and added that profits were likely to continue to rise in future.

Chief executive Ulrich Geissmann told reporters at a press club meeting in Stuttgart on Wednesday evening that the company expected to post a group profit of 18 million Swiss francs this year, an increase of 2.8 million francs from the previous year.
Operating profit was expected to grow by 600 million francs to 27 million, he added.
Looking ahead to future years, Geissmann said, "We will also be able to further increase profits in the future. Of this, I am certain."

Geissmann declined to give any long-term forecasts on likely developments in the company's sales, but said 1996 turnover was likely to rise to 796.5 million francs from 793.7 million, including the Schoeller ice cream business.
Excluding Schoeller, sales would edge up to 441.14 million francs from 440.6 million, Geissmann said.
Germany is Moevenpick's second largest market after Switzerland.
